0.0.n: This is Mandarin Chinese, used with 好 to greet a group.

0.1.n: In Mandarin 大家好, 好 completes the greeting; its basic meaning is good.

0.3.n: This is the Mandarin first-person pronoun, not the usual Japanese 私.

0.4.n: This is Mandarin, linking 我 to the speaker’s name.

0.6.n: This Japanese polite ending follows the name, playfully mixing Japanese with Mandarin.

1.0.n: Sets the time for presenting the vlog, not for the five years of employment.

1.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic of the announcement.

1.2.n: 年 counts years and here gives the length of employment.

1.3.n: Follows the duration to make it approximate.

1.4.n: Past form of 勤める, describing employment at the school named in the next line.

2.0.n: Combines with 学校 to describe what the school teaches.

2.1.n: The preceding 5年くらい勤めた describes this school as the place where the speaker worked.

2.2.n: Links the school to the last day of attending work there.

2.3.n: Refers to going in to work, here forming a phrase with 最終日.

2.4.n: Combines 最終, final, with 日, day.

2.5.n: Links the last workday to the vlog documenting it.

2.6.n: An English borrowing for a video diary.

2.7.n: Marks the vlog as what the speaker will present.

2.8.n: お plus the stem of 届ける combines with します for a humble expression directed toward viewers.

2.9.n: Polite form of する; with お届け, it completes the promise to present the vlog.

3.0.n: The speaker explicitly identifies herself as the topic.

3.1.n: Marks 私 as the topic of the employment explanation.

3.2.n: Describes a non-full-time position; teacher is understood from the school context.

3.3.n: This is the shortened part of だ used before た to form だった.

3.4.n: Combines with だっ to make だった, the plain past form of だ.

3.5.n: Introduces the reason the speaker did not attend work every day.

4.0.n: The following negative expression denies that this was the work schedule.

4.1.n: Part of ではない, the negative form of だ; it is not a location marker here.

4.2.n: Within ではない, は helps contrast daily attendance with the actual schedule.

4.3.n: Makes ではない negative; the form is nonpast even though the surrounding story concerns past employment.

4.4.n: Makes the negative statement polite without adding a separate action.

4.5.n: Connects this qualification to the higher attendance frequency described next.

5.0.n: Describes times when the speaker’s work attendance was higher, not necessarily when the school was busy.

5.1.n: 多い modifies 時 directly to mean occasions with more frequent attendance.

5.2.n: Marks 多い時 as the situation being discussed.

5.3.n: Before a frequency count, 週 gives the period over which occurrences are counted.

5.4.n: 回 counts occurrences; here these are trips in to work.

5.5.n: 出勤する in the ていました form politely describes a repeated past routine.

0.lit: Everyone, hello; I am Shaji, am.
0.tip: The greeting and 我是 are Mandarin Chinese, while です is a Japanese polite ending.

1.lit: Today, as for, approximately five years worked at…
1.tip: 勤めた describes 日本語学校 in the next line, so the phrase continues across the subtitle break.

2.lit: Japanese-language school’s work-attendance last day’s vlog, I will present.
2.tip: The two の particles connect the school, its last workday, and the vlog into one long phrase.

3.lit: I, as for, was part-time, because…
3.tip: ので gives the reason for the next statement: the speaker did not work every day.

4.lit: It is not every day, but…
4.tip: ではないです is a polite negative expression; が links it to a contrasting detail.

5.lit: At frequent times, four times per week I was attending work.
5.tip: ていました describes a repeated past routine here, rather than one action in progress.
